Q1_best_normal_33_37.question: Best feasible operating condition under the normal 33-37 C constraint (max margin per cycle time)

Q2_best_min36.question: Best feasible condition when the minimum temperature is 36 C (36-37 C)

Q3_model_change.question: Does the preferred condition change when M2 or M6 is used instead of M5?

Q4_best_margin.question: Which candidate has the best estimated margin per cycle time?
Q4_best_margin.note: Computed over every completed feasible grid point; unfinished and out-of-curve points are excluded by construction.

Q5_fastest_completion.question: Which candidate reaches the TRS completion threshold fastest?
Q5_fastest_completion.note: Fastest is not the most profitable: the lowest sugar charge finishes first but gives up margin per cycle time.

Q6_high_margin_feasibility.question: Are the highest-margin candidates feasible under the batch-completion requirement?
Q6_high_margin_feasibility.answer: Every candidate that is ranked is completed (TRS <= 5 g/L) and inside the steam curve. The candidates with the most ethanol at 120 h are all outside the 7-14 % v/v curve, so none of them can be priced or recommended.

Q7_unfinished_effect.question: What happens to the optimum if some candidates fail to reach TRS <= 5 g/L?
Q7_unfinished_effect.answer: Unfinished candidates are recorded with their state at 120 h but receive no completion time, no ethanol end point and no margin, so they cannot enter the ranking. Extending the horizon to 240 h only confirms this: none of the unfinished candidates would beat the recommended point, and the extension is not used to rank.

Q8_uncertainty.question: How sensitive is the recommendation to parameter and model uncertainty?
Q8_uncertainty.answer: The recommended condition stays completed and inside the steam curve in every draw, but the margin per cycle time carries a finite interval; the discrete assumption alternatives move it far less than the parameter ensemble.

Q9_most_influential_assumptions.question: Which assumptions most affect the recommendation?
items: The completion criterion is binding: every sugar charge above ~200-210 g/L either finishes late or leaves the steam curve, so the optimum sits just above 190 g/L rather than where ethanol is highest.
The steam curve limits the usable wash strength to 14 % v/v (about 110 g/L ethanol): high-sugar, high-ethanol batches cannot be costed at all.
The 37 C rate multiplier rests on one run (R8), so the 36-37 C scenario is the least supported part of the surface.
The temperature multipliers are piecewise-linear between 30/34/37 C, so a 33 C prediction is an interpolation assumption, not a measurement.
The CO2 standard-deviation floor (0.10 g/L) changes the parameter covariance and therefore the width of every interval.

Q10_additional_experiment.question: What additional experiment or data would most reduce decision uncertainty?
Q10_additional_experiment.answer: A single batch at the recommended condition (about 195 g/L TRS, 33 C) run past 48 h to the TRS <= 5 g/L endpoint, because it simultaneously tests the completion time that drives the margin-per-cycle-time metric and the growth/production behaviour in the 33 C region that the plant now operates in. A second 37 C run would help the warm scenario but cannot fix the 33 C gap.

brief_Q5_37C_260.question: Brief Q5: what does the model predict at 37 C and 260 g/L, and how far is it trustworthy?
brief_Q5_37C_260.trust: LOW: one 37 C run only (R8, 220 g/L), no 37 C / 260 g/L observation, a 120 h prediction against 48 h of data, and ethanol above 105 g/L while the fitted P_max is 195.0 g/L (for M5 the inhibition exponent is entangled with P_max). It is reported because the brief asks for it; it is not an operating recommendation.

brief_Q6_experiment.question: Brief Q6: which single additional experiment would most reduce the uncertainty that matters?
brief_Q6_experiment.answer: The same recommendation as Q10: one extended batch at the proposed plant condition (~195 g/L TRS at 33 C) taken to the 5 g/L endpoint, ideally with a mid-run 60-96 h sample, because the decision is limited by the time-to-completion extrapolation rather than by the 48 h kinetics.
